problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-x(y-1)^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>1$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<1$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/ef935d673ddc4fa3b66305717f495914c194be2abff63611f8f6be6763e469ce.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/6f2f29dbb53e8c20d963cc48c89af73b1c806985bc77842cbe28b882305ede32.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-x$ | $(y-1)^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,2)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,2)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,0)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/71aceb11f3056308300e3e5c9587d76a281379964caab83f640a6924ffd94298.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>1$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<1$ | $+$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
